title: fix(plugin-form): merge `initialData` over `initialValues` per member
body:
Fixes #9760

`Clause-②: no`

Maintainer ruling, batch #166 item 3, letter 甲: one shared helper replaces the
whole-object `schema.initialData || schema.initialValues` at every read site, so
`initialData` merges PER MEMBER over `initialValues` — exactly what its published
description ("alternate spelling … read FIRST") says. The description's promise is
unchanged; the code now keeps it.

## The corpus, measured rather than inherited

Base ref `00c4df509c09634650932070d08f1f27e2fa2857` (`origin/main`, re-read
2026-09-18T19:10:03Z — identical to the tip the dispatch named). Probe run
2026-09-18T19:10:56Z, repo-wide, printing lines rather than a count:

```
git grep -nE "initialData\s*\|\|" -- .
```

⇒ **12 EXECUTABLE sites in 6 files**, every one of them in `packages/plugin-form/src`:

| file | sites | shape |
|---|---|---|
| `DrawerForm.tsx` | 2 | `seedCreateValues(...)` + `setFormData(... \|\| {})` |
| `ModalForm.tsx` | 2 | same pair |
| `ObjectForm.tsx` | 2 | `setInitialData(... \|\| {})` twice — no `seedCreateValues` on this arm |
| `SplitForm.tsx` | 2 | same pair as Drawer/Modal |
| `TabbedForm.tsx` | 1 | `seedCreateValues(...)` only |
| `WizardForm.tsx` | 3 | `seedCreateValues(...)` ×3 |

Every other hit the probe returned is prose: two `.changeset/` bodies, one
`CHANGELOG.md` paragraph, four test docblocks, three `pins` ledger strings in
`apps/console`, and `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx`'s registration
**description**.

### ⚠️ Where my number differs from the ruling's, stated plainly

The ruling says **13 sites across 7 files**. I measure **12 executable sites across
6 files**. The two reconcile only if the registration description at
`packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` is counted as the 13th site and that file as
the 7th — which is how the dispatch's own enumeration read it. On that reading the
ruling's count is right and nothing is missing; on a code-only reading it is 12/6.

**`MasterDetailForm.tsx` is NOT a site**, and the dispatch's candidate for the 7th
file is wrong in a way worth recording. It never spells the choice: its
`parentSchema` memo copies `initialValues` and `initialData` key by key onto an
`object-form`-shaped object rendered through a directly imported `ObjectForm`, so
it inherits the repair rather than needing one. It is, as the dispatch suspected, a
**producer of the empty object** — its expanded-row form authors
`initialData: expandedRow ?? {}` — but that producer needed no edit either: with no
`initialValues` beside it, `{ ...{}, ...expandedRow }` and `expandedRow || ...` agree.
It is left untouched and its behaviour is pinned through the flipped pin below.

## What changed

- **`packages/plugin-form/src/initialRecord.ts` (new).** `resolveInitialRecord(schema)`
  returns `{ ...(schema.initialValues ?? {}), ...(schema.initialData ?? {}) }` — always
  a fresh plain object, never nullish, never either authored object by reference.
- **All 12 sites route through it.** ⛔ No arm keeps the `||`; the residual probe over
  `packages/plugin-form/src/*.ts{,x}` returns prose only, with the helper's own 12 call
  sites + 6 imports firing as the same-command control.
- **Both read shapes are routed AND measured.** The ruling said triage had not verified
  they are semantically identical. They are **not**, and the difference is not the merge:
  - the create branches spell `seedCreateValues(objectSchema, resolveInitialRecord(schema), ctx)`,
    which keeps the object schema's declared `defaultValue`s UNDERNEATH the merge (objectui#4047);
  - the direct installs spell `setFormData(resolveInitialRecord(schema))` with nothing underneath.
  `seedCreateValues` is `{ ...schemaDefaultValues(...), ...(initial ?? {}) }`, so handing it
  `{}` where it used to get `undefined` is a no-op by construction — but the DEFAULTS LAYER
  is a real behavioural difference between the two shapes, and it is now pinned on both sides
  (rows 3 and 6 of the new file) so that "unifying" the arms by dropping `seedCreateValues`
  goes red instead of silently un-fixing objectui#4047.
- **`objectui#9759`'s pin flips, ⛔ nothing deleted.** Rows 3 and 4 of
  `objectFormInitialMembers-8071.test.tsx` now assert the merge, with the reason written into
  the file: they were written deliberately against the old behaviour by a pins-only card.
- **⚠️ A SECOND pin flips, which this dispatch did not name.**
  `masterDetailInitialMembers-8071.test.tsx` rows 3 and 4 record the same two facts one layer
  up, inherited through the `parentSchema` memo. They are flipped the same way, with the same
  reason recorded. Had they been left alone this branch would simply have gone red.
- **Changeset** `@object-ui/plugin-form` **minor**, carrying the behaviour note the ruling
  dictates.

### Two edits that go slightly beyond the ruling's letter — flagged, ⛔ not slipped in

1. **`index.tsx`'s two registration descriptions.** The ruling says the description is
   unchanged, and its PROMISE is: "alternate spelling … read FIRST" and "prefer `initialValues`
   in new schemas" are untouched. But both strings also QUOTED the expression this change
   deletes — `object-form.initialData` carried `` (`schema.initialData || schema.initialValues`) ``
   and `object-master-detail-form.initialData` carried the cross-file line address
   `(MasterDetailForm.tsx:602)`. Shipping either would put authoring-facing metadata in front of
   users citing code that no longer exists. Only those two citations are replaced, by the
   per-member statement and by a content citation respectively. ⭐ The line address was also
   already false on its own terms: that address is a `console.warn` about child-schema loading,
   unrelated to either key — the AGENTS.md rule against cross-file line addresses, repaired
   opportunistically in a file this change touches anyway. If the seat reads the ruling more
   literally, reverting these two strings is a one-line revert each and nothing else depends on them.
2. **`apps/console`'s member-pin ledger prose.** Three `pins` strings in
   `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` describe the pin files this change flips, and each says
   the behaviour was "recorded … and handed back as a finding rather than fixed". This change
   makes those sentences false about the very files they cite, so they are updated to describe
   what is pinned now, naming the flip. Nothing mechanical reads that prose — which is exactly
   why a stale one would never go red.

## Ablation — the fix's own pin proved able to fail

Mutation: `resolveInitialRecord`'s body swapped back to
`return schema?.initialData || schema?.initialValues || {};`, cast back to the module's declared
return type (angle brackets are spelled out here because this body's sanitizer eats tag-shaped fragments)
Anchored replacement with a hit-count assertion in both directions, `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`
with absolute paths, restore via `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`. Run against commit
`4309ef173`.

```
HEAD blob for packages/plugin-form/src/initialRecord.ts = 67dc03fad1393bc755d38dcdfda6251c09c6acf3
pre-mutation working blob    = 67dc03fad1393bc755d38dcdfda6251c09c6acf3
BEFORE  merge-line hits: 1   whole-object-line hits: 0
AFTER   merge-line hits: 0   whole-object-line hits: 1
post-mutation working blob   = 6b1408750465e57271ce8c14fb49facc1bb34dd2
mutated-leg vitest exit = 1
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  23 failed | 15 passed (38)
post-restore working blob    = 67dc03fad1393bc755d38dcdfda6251c09c6acf3
git diff HEAD after restore  = []
RESTORED merge-line hits: 1   whole-object-line hits: 0
restored-leg vitest exit = 0
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

The restore leg is proved twice over — blob hash equality with the HEAD blob AND an empty
`git diff HEAD` — and by the hit counts, not by the exit code of a step that exits 0 when it
does nothing.

**The inputs the two implementations disagree about** are the only ones the behavioural rows use:
an EMPTY `initialData` beside a populated `initialValues`, and a PARTIAL `initialData` naming one
member of several. The 15 rows that stay GREEN under the mutation are the controls — the
single-key rows, the no-keys rows, and the master-detail block's own batch/edit rows — which is
what keeps the 23 reds from being a file that simply broke.

## Verification

Run through the shared seat lock (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=1`), from the repo root.

| what | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| dependency closure | `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` | exit 0 |
| plugin-form, whole package | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` | `Test Files 101 passed (101)` · `Tests 965 passed \| 1 skipped (966)` |
| console parity ledger | `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 199 passed (199)` |
| typecheck | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --filter @object-ui/console type-check` | exit 0 (plugin-form's `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` half covers the test files) |

Gates, each read from its own verdict line with the exit code captured before any pipe:
`check:new-line-citations` · `check:control-bytes` · `check:unreferenced-sources` ·
`check:component-surface-parity` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` ·
`check:test-path-roots` · `check:entry-guard` · `check:comment-mask-corpus` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` ·
`check:vi-mock-inherit` · `check:vi-mock-override-shape` · `check:lint-rule-coverage` ·
`check:registry-bare-names` · `check:doc-types` · `check:prompt-keys` ·
`check:element-data-source-declaration` · `check:action-ref-convention` · `check:shell-escape-residue` ·
`check:changeset-presence` — all exit 0.

`check:sdui-registration-pins` and `check:readme-exports` first returned exit 2 and exit 1 with
PREREQUISITE-NOT-MET verdicts ("No console build to weigh", "type entry not on disk"). Both were
re-run after building `@object-ui/console`, `@object-ui/cli` and `@object-ui/plugin-ai` and both
then exit 0 — recorded because the first readings are ⛔ not failures and ⛔ not passes.

`check:governed-queue-guard --test` over all 13 changed paths: **NOT GOVERNED**, 0 of 5 surfaces matched.

### Lint — a DECLARED narrowing, with the three things that make it a measurement

Run at final head (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`: `4309ef173`), over every `.ts`/`.tsx` file in the
diff: **0 errors, 190 warnings** (all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and
`react-refresh/only-export-components`, matching the surrounding code — `ObjectFormSchema` itself
types both keys as a string-keyed record of `any`).

1. **The population is read from eslint's own config**, not guessed: `eslint.config.js` applies its
   TS block to `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` under one repo-root `ignores` list.
2. **The file count is read from `--format json`**: 12 files linted — every `.ts`/`.tsx` path in the diff.
3. **Invariance for untouched files**: no type-aware linting is configured (no `projectService`, no
   `project:`, no TS program in `languageOptions`), and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the
   filesystem (`grep -rnE "require\('fs'\)|from 'fs'|readFileSync|readdirSync|globSync"` over that
   directory returns nothing, with a live control on the same directory in the same command). Every
   file's verdict is therefore computed from that file's own source alone ⇒ this diff cannot move the
   verdict of a file it does not contain. The repo-wide run remains CI's.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, noted, ⛔ not filed

- `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` carries two further cross-file line addresses on keys this card
  does not touch: `object-form.modalCloseButton` cites `ObjectForm.tsx:361` and
  `object-form.contentLayout` cites `ModalForm.tsx:638`. Same banned form as the one repaired above,
  but on unrelated keys — repairing them here would be the sweep the rule forbids. Successor: the next
  PR that edits either description.
- `object-form.initialData`'s description still says "the drawer/modal presentations read FIRST". Every
  presentation reads it, including the flat `ObjectForm` — a pre-existing narrowing this change neither
  created nor widened, left alone because the ruling holds the description's wording. Successor: the
  next card that re-words that description.

## Seat correction, appended after the merge-queue ejection and the rework

Written by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat at **2026-09-18T21:02Z** (clock read by this write). A dev writes its PR body once and ⛔ never PATCHes it, so the two repairs it named in its second report are made here.

**(a) One load-bearing sentence in this body is FALSE and is replaced.** Where it says the two read shapes differ because the direct installs 「have no defaults layer」, read instead:

> both shapes layer the object schema's declared `defaultValues` under the authored record, at different sites — the sectioned arms at seed time through `seedCreateValues`, the flat form one composition later at render as `{ ...schemaDefaults, ...initialData }`; neither layers an inline `customFields` member's own `defaultValue`.

⭐ The dev found this **itself**, and the way it found it is worth keeping: after merging `origin/main` in, **three rows of its own new pin went RED**. The 「no defaults layer」 reading had been an **artefact of the probe** — the inline-customFields path used to install a members-only `{ name, fields: {} }` schema and never fetch the object's, so `schemaDefaultValues` returned `{}` by construction. objectui#9778 (merged into main after this branch was cut) made that path MERGE over the generated set, the real metadata arrives, and the declared default duly appeared. ⛔ No row was skipped, disabled or deleted; the pin and the changeset now say what is measured.

**(b) Every number in this body's Verification and Ablation tables was taken at the PRE-MERGE head `4309ef173`.** They are superseded by the merged-head re-runs at `427528f15`, recorded in the second `os-dev-report` on objectui#9760 (`5736125661`): `packages/plugin-form/` 967 passed | 1 skipped; the ablation 24 red / 15 green under mutation, 39 green restored; eslint 191 warnings, 0 errors.

⚠️ **A correction the seat owes on its own ejection dispatch:** it named the colliding file and the colliding commit correctly and was **incomplete about the cost** — the textual conflict was one small hunk, and the expensive half was **semantic and invisible to git**: objectui#9778 changed what the inline path fetches, which falsified three assertions in a file it never touched. A conflict round that stopped at 「no markers left, it compiles」 would have pushed a red branch.
